entries.definition: The watcher-tree and the priesthood's sign — first tree to wake, from shaqad, to watch: “I will watch over my word.” Aaron's dead rod budded, blossomed, and yielded almonds overnight — the house of Levi chosen by a resurrection sign — and the sanctuary lampstand is carved of almond cups: the watcher-tree bears the lamp.
entries.citations: (Jer 1:11-12; Num 17:8; Ex 25:33-34) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.term: Assembly of the wicked / synagogue of Satan
entries.definition: The counterfeit congregation — an edah (the covenant-assembly word) claiming covenant standing while gathered against the covenant's Lord: God names the rebel camp “this evil congregation… gathered together against me,” Korah's company declares all the congregation holy, and at the cross the assembly encloses the Messiah from inside the camp while the dogs compass from without — “the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not.”
entries.citations: (Ps 22:16; Num 14:35; 16:3; Ps 1:5; 26:5; Acts 4:27; Rev 2:9; 3:9) · see What Is the Point?, ch. 25

entries.definition: The self-made kingdom that builds a name against heaven — an empire raised over many kingdoms, the covenant counterfeit.
entries.citations: (Gen 11:4; Jer 51:7; Rev 17:18) · see The Bow, ch. 44, and The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The firstfruits — the first and humblest grain, reaped in spring; the sheaf waved before the LORD, which is Christ risen.
entries.citations: (Ex 9:31; Lev 23:10; Ruth 1:22; 2 Kgs 4:42; 1 Cor 15:20) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: A nation or kingdom of the world — the wild, predatory figure of a people, as the tree is its rooted figure; different beasts are different kingdoms, and the unclean beasts are the Gentile nations God cleanses in Peter's vision.

What a people is strung together by — a kingdom's covenant, and the might that is that covenant's outward face: one word (qesheth) carries weapon, might, and covenant-token, and to break the bow is to unstring the kingdom.
The curse-ground's crop — those consumed by “the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches”: fruitless, choking the word, offering a false shadow, and ending in fire.
entries.citations: (Gen 3:18; Matt 13:22; Judg 9:15; 2 Sam 23:6-7; Heb 6:8) · see The Parables of the Kingdom, ch. 2

entries.definition: The members of a nation — broken off, or grafted in, while the tree itself stands.
entries.citations: (Rom 11:17) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: The word of God.
entries.citations: (Deut 8:3; Matt 4:4) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: The word churned solid — milk worked by labor into sound doctrine: the diet that teaches to “refuse the evil, and choose the good,” the remnant's food, the wash of the walking feet (“I washed my steps with butter”). Its counterfeit is speech “smoother than butter” with war beneath.
entries.citations: (Prov 30:33; Isa 7:15, 22; Job 29:6; 2 Sam 17:29; Ps 55:21) · see Butter, ch. 47

entries.term: Cast into the sea (a stone, mountain, or millstone sinking)
entries.definition: The fall of Babylon — a ruling power irreversibly destroyed, sunk into the sea of peoples, never to rise. A phrase-symbol, not a single word.
entries.citations: (Jer 51:63-64; Rev 18:21; Ex 15:4-5) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The towering tree — a power of great height and majesty, whoever bears it: Assyria was “a cedar in Lebanon”; the house of David the “high cedar” whose tender twig God replants to become “a goodly cedar”; the righteous “grow like a cedar.” The symbol is the stature, not the nation's identity.
The empty husk winnowed off the grain and driven away by the wind — what the wicked are likened to: weightless, rootless, blown off and burned. Not to be confused with the tares.
entries.citations: (Ps 1:4; Matt 3:12) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: The vehicle of heaven — “who maketh the clouds his chariot” — and its cargo is the word: “my doctrine shall drop as the rain.” The pillar that led Israel, the cloud that received Him and brings Him back in like manner, the transport of the caught-up saints; risen from the sea of peoples, a multitude airborne — the cloud of witnesses. Its counterfeit is the cloud without water.
entries.citations: (Ps 104:3; Ex 13:21; Acts 1:9-11; Dan 7:13; 1 Thess 4:17; Heb 12:1) · see Clouds, ch. 37 | (Ps 104:3; Ex 13:21; Acts 1:9-11; Dan 7:13; 1 Thess 4:17; Heb 12:1) · see Clouds, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The stamped image — a person as the owner's minted image-bearer: dug from the field, refined in the fire, struck with the NAME; priced by the law, ransomed at a flat half-shekel when counted, lost and sought by lamplight. Man's mint valued the Shepherd at slave-damages; God's scales weigh the widow's whole living above all abundance.
Concealed disobedience — deeds hidden from the light.
entries.citations: (John 3:19-20) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: The time of light — exposure and accountability, when deeds are seen and tested; the season to walk, work, and watch. The children of light are the children of the day. In the prophets’ counts the day is a unit that scales: a day for a year in judgment, and one day with the Lord as a thousand years.
entries.citations: (Gen 1:5; John 9:4; 1 Thess 5:5; Num 14:34; Ezek 4:6; 2 Pet 3:8) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: One in whom the law is sealed — “seal the law among my disciples” — proven by continuing in the word, love, and fruit; three times Jesus says cannot of those who will not leave their own, bear the cross, and forsake all. Baptized into the Name, the disciple is perfected “as his master” — the Head whose Name carries the Word, the covenant law, and the fruitful priesthood.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: a learner and follower of Jesus — any believer, entered by faith and baptism, growing lifelong in Christlikeness.
entries.citations: (Isa 8:16; Luke 6:40; Ex 23:21; Jer 31:33; John 8:31; Luke 14:26-33; Rev 14:1) · see The Disciple, ch. 9

entries.definition: The covenant lawsuit executed — the wife sent out of the house: exile and scattering. Hated when it betrays the wife of the covenant; commanded when the union is itself fornication — a marriage God never joined. God gave Israel the bill, and answered His own no-return rule at the cross.
entries.citations: (Jer 3:8; Isa 50:1; Deut 24:1-4; Ezra 10:3; Mal 2:11-16) · see Marriage and Divorce, ch. 12

entries.definition: The Gentile power — an unclean beast outside the covenant table, fed on the crumbs that fall from it until brought in; at the cross it was the dogs that compassed and pierced, and at the end, without are dogs.
entries.citations: (Matt 15:26-27; Mark 7:28; Ps 22:16; Rev 22:15) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: The destination of the way — the entrance to the house of God, marked on the posts.
entries.citations: (Ex 12:7; Deut 6:9; John 10:9) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7

entries.definition: A devouring kingdom.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: Satan himself, per Revelation 12:9.
entries.citations: (Pharaoh, Ezek 29:3; Babylon, Jer 51:34) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: The front of the compass — Hebrew qedem, “east” and “ancient” in one word: Eden planted eastward, the glory returning “from the way of the east,” the lightning of the coming, the kings of the east crossing the dried river. Where beginnings and returns come from.
entries.citations: (Gen 2:8; Ezek 43:2; Matt 24:27; Rev 16:12; Ezek 46:1) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: Spiritually, the whore of Babylon that rides the beast — the city that kills the prophets, “where also our Lord was crucified”: Jerusalem.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: bondage to sin, and the world-system out of which God redeems.
entries.citations: (Rev 11:8; 18:24; Matt 23:37; Gal 4:25; Isa 1:10) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: Babel’s confederate — allied with Shinar in Scripture's first war, judged under Babylon's own sentence (“I will break the bow of Elam”), its oracle the prologue to Babylon's fall.
entries.citations: (Gen 14:1, 9; Jer 49:35; 51:56) · see The Bow, ch. 44

entries.definition: The leaders of the assemblies, seated among the host of heaven — the court round about the throne, the named and brightest of the stars.
entries.citations: (1 Kgs 22:19; Isa 24:23; Rev 4:4; Matt 19:28; Ps 89:5-7) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: The scattered firstborn whose seed becomes the fulness of the nations.
entries.citations: (Gen 48:19) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The lamp of the body — a burning light within a person, shining as the stars shine; the good eye gives its bread to the poor, the evil eye withholds; His eyes are flames of fire, running to and fro through all the earth.
entries.citations: (Matt 6:22-23; Prov 22:9; 23:6; Zech 4:10; Rev 1:14; 5:6) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: The Messiah — the one who bears the Father's light unchanged through the night; the moon is that name written in the sky, His throne established in the heavens.
entries.citations: (Ps 89:37; Rev 1:5; 3:14; Isa 55:4) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: God's covenant people left without their Father — the remnant.
entries.citations: (Lam 5:3) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: Reverent awe expressed as keeping the commandments and departing from evil.
entries.citations: (Eccl 12:13) · see The Fear of the Lord, ch. 23

entries.definition: The walk — a man's conduct, his way; washed clean while the body stays bathed.
entries.citations: (John 13:10) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

entries.definition: Self-made righteousness — a covering of one's own cut, all show and no substance; the cursed fig tree bore leaves but no fruit.
entries.citations: (Gen 3:7; Matt 21:19) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

entries.definition: The world — Jesus’ own decoding — sown with the seed of the word and reaped at the harvest; its unreaped edge is where the poor and stranger glean, and its hidden treasure is bought whole to be mined.
entries.citations: (Matt 13:38; Lev 19:9-10) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: God's own consuming presence — “the LORD thy God is a consuming fire”: never a chamber, always the encounter. The same fire sustains the bush, refines the silver, walks the covered out of the furnace, and consumes the uncovered; the difference is never the fire but the covering.
entries.citations: (Deut 4:24; Heb 12:29; Ex 3:2; Dan 3:25-27; Mal 3:3; 1 Cor 3:15) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition: The divider God set between the two seas of people — the restless nations below and the gathered waters above, the heavenly assembly — and the place where the lights are hung.
entries.citations: (Gen 1:6-8, 14-17; Ps 148:4; Rev 17:15) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: Men in the sea of nations — and the redeemed drawn out of it, the catch of the fishers of men gathered in the net.
entries.citations: (Hab 1:14; Matt 4:19; 13:47-48) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: A great ruler among the sea of peoples — the personal head who can stand for the kingdom, state, and administration acting through him. Pharaoh stands for Egypt, Nebuchadnezzar for Babylon, and Caesar for Rome: the ruler swallows through the body he heads, and is forced to give back what he swallowed.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: God's appointed rescue-instrument, a type of the three days in the tomb.
entries.citations: (Ezek 29:3; 32:2; Jer 51:34, 44; Dan 7:17, 23; John 19:15-16) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: An army in motion — a nation invading, or the Lord's own host sweeping the enemy away.
entries.citations: (Isa 8:7; Jer 47:2; Dan 9:26) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: One who hears God's word and will not do it — the lawless, not the unintelligent.
entries.citations: (Ps 14:1; Matt 7:26) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: The blocking flesh — “the body of the sins of the flesh,” Scripture's own decode — covering a covenant member and stopping its work: the uncircumcised heart cannot be humbled or love, the uncircumcised ear “cannot hearken,” uncircumcised lips cannot be heard, and a young tree's fruit is “uncircumcised” until the covenant year. Cut it away, or be cut off.
Spiritual unfaithfulness — breaking covenant with God to go after other gods and kingdoms; not merely the physical sin. The out-of-covenant union is itself the whoredom.
entries.citations: (Ex 34:15-16; Hos 1:2; Jer 3:9; Rev 17:2) · see Marriage and Divorce, ch. 12

entries.definition: The four spirits of heaven — God's executing agents, shown as the four horsemen.
entries.citations: (Zech 6:5) · see The Four Winds, ch. 34

entries.definition: A nation's works, by which it is judged — “every good tree bringeth forth good fruit”.
entries.citations: (Matt 7:17; 21:43) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: A planted stand of trees — a grouping of nations.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: paradise and fellowship with God — Eden lost and restored.
entries.citations: (Ezek 31:9) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: Righteousness — the righteous acts of the saints.
entries.citations: (Rev 19:8, ASV) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

entries.definition: The judgment — the valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem's wall, where the carcases of the transgressors burn: “their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.” What destroys “both soul and body,” distinct from Sheol, the grave that holds all alike.
entries.citations: (Matt 10:28; Isa 66:24; Jer 7:32; Mark 9:43-48) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition: The rage of the wicked at the righteous — what the excluded do at the sight of the kingdom they forfeited, sorrow and hatred in one face; then they melt away. Defined on the wicked against the just, staged at Stephen's trial, templated in the psalm: he shall see, be grieved, gnash, and perish.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the anguish of the damned under conscious, everlasting torment.
entries.citations: (Ps 112:10; Ps 37:12; Luke 13:28; Acts 7:54; Matt 8:12) · see The Weeping and the Gnashing | (Ps 112:10; Ps 37:12; Luke 13:28; Acts 7:54; Matt 8:12) · see The Weeping and the Gnashing, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The gospel of the kingdom — the renewed covenant, the law going forth from Zion.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the good news that Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again.
entries.citations: (Isa 52:7; 2:3; Jer 31:33; Heb 4:2) · see Gospel, ch. 5

entries.definition: The wild branch — the stranger, the Gentile — received into the covenant tree.
entries.citations: (Rom 11:17) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: A nation's works ripened into its people — persons as the vineyard's yield: God looked for grapes — judgment and righteousness — and found men: Israel “like grapes in the wilderness,” the good man the missing cluster, the remnant the blessing left in it. Pressed, the grape gives blood — the cup of the covenant, or the cup of wrath, as the vintage is grapes or wild grapes.
entries.citations: (Isa 5:2-7; Hos 9:10; Mic 7:1-2; Isa 65:8; Gen 49:11; Rev 14:18-20) · see The Parable of the Vineyard | (Isa 5:2-7; Hos 9:10; Mic 7:1-2; Isa 65:8; Gen 49:11; Rev 14:18-20) · see The Parable of the Vineyard, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The individual mortal — a man, flesh; and the field God farms unto harvest.
entries.citations: (Isa 40:6-8; Matt 13:38) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: The covenant-breaker who wears the form of covenant without its substance — “that great city,” spiritually Sodom, Egypt, Babylon: Jerusalem unfaithful.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: spiritual adultery; in Revelation, an apostate religious world-system — Rome, not Jerusalem.
entries.citations: (Rev 17:18; 11:8; Ezek 23:19) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The end of the age, when the field of mankind is reaped — the wheat gathered, the chaff burned.
entries.citations: (Joel 3:13; Matt 13:39) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: Jerusalem — the navel and heart of the land.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the grave or Hades, where Christ lay three days.
entries.citations: (Matt 12:40; Ezek 5:5; 38:12) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4, and The Ship

entries.definition: The jurisdiction where God's will is already done — the visible sky and the seat of rule in one dual word (shamayim), over against the earth, the realm delegated to men where His will must yet be done. God's motion is downward — rain, fire, the Son, the city; the climb up is Babel's. The hope is heaven come down, not man gone up.
entries.citations: (Ps 115:16; Isa 66:1; Matt 6:10; John 3:13; Rev 21:2-3) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition: One English word laid over two different things — Sheol/Hades, the grave that swallows righteous and wicked alike, and Gehenna, the judgment that destroys. The doctrine changes with the word beneath.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the place of eternal conscious punishment and separation from God.
entries.citations: (Ps 16:10 with Matt 10:28) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition: The head covered with yeshuah — Yeshua: God's own war-dress, put on when there was no man, and lent to the soldier; David's form of it — “thou hast covered my head in the day of battle.” The head of every man is Christ, and the counterfeit is issued for the same forehead.
entries.citations: (Isa 59:16-17; Eph 6:11, 17; Ps 140:7; 1 Cor 11:3; 1 Thess 5:8; Rev 22:4) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

entries.definition: The way of holiness — the prepared road home.
entries.citations: (Isa 35:8) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7

entries.definition: The mount of an executing spirit; the conqueror who wins the nations by the bow.
entries.citations: (Rev 6:2) · see The Four Winds, ch. 34

entries.term: Image of metals (gold, silver, brass, clay)
entries.definition: The succession of gentile world-kingdoms, shattered by the stone-kingdom of God.
entries.citations: (Dan 2:32-45) · see Mountain, ch. 39

entries.definition: The discipline of the law, received and kept — what only fools despise.
entries.citations: (Prov 1:7; 23:23) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: The fourth kingdom — Rome: Daniel named Medo-Persia and Greece outright, and the iron that breaks in pieces all before it is the empire that held the world when He came.
entries.citations: (Dan 2:40; 8:20-21) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: A set-apart, sanctified people — the covenant-rock risen out of the sea of nations (a mountain breaking the surface), waiting for the law that sanctifies it; “the island of the innocent,” delivered to safety while the kingdoms fall.
The new name of the one who prevails with God — covenant and character, not blood.
entries.citations: (Gen 32:28; Rom 9:6) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The crooked, supplanting human heart that God transforms.
entries.citations: (Gen 27:36; Jer 17:9) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: In covenant contexts, one in the covenant — “he is a Jew, which is one inwardly,” while some “say they are Jews, and are not.” The name is Judah's, and Judah means praise — “Now will I praise the LORD” — so Paul's definition lands on the name itself: the Jew inwardly is he “whose praise is not of men, but of God.” The word also walks in plain dress, ethnic and religious; context decides which coat it wears.
entries.citations: (Rom 2:28-29; Gen 29:35; Rev 3:9; Rom 9:6; Zech 8:23) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The law's ruling and the ruler's office — what God declares due, kept like a commandment and owed first to the widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor. To judge is to rule and deliver by the law (the judges were saviours; “a king to judge us… and fight our battles”), so the righteous pray for judgment and creation rejoices at its coming; condemnation is one verdict of the office, not the office.
entries.citations: (Deut 10:18; Ps 119:160; Matt 23:23; 1 Sam 8:20; Isa 33:22; Dan 7:22) · see Justice and Judgment, ch. 18

entries.definition: Righteousness under a second English name — one Hebrew word behind both renderings: the commandments done where a neighbor can be wronged or righted.
entries.citations: (Gen 18:19/Jer 22:3; Ps 89:14/97:2) · see Justice and Judgment, ch. 18

entries.definition: Covenant relationship proven by obedience — the intimate “knew” of marriage; a stranger is one not known.
entries.citations: (Gen 4:1; Hos 4:6; Matt 7:23; 1 John 2:3-4) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: One of the flock — a covenant person, not by itself Christ: Nathan's ewe lamb is a poor man's beloved, Jeremiah is “like a lamb… brought to the slaughter,” the disciples are sent “as lambs among wolves.” The Lamb of God is Christ — the one lamb “without blemish,” taken “out from the sheep”: the perfect lamb of the flock.
entries.citations: (2 Sam 12:3; Jer 11:19; Isa 53:6-7; Ex 12:5; Luke 10:3; John 1:29) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The commandment.
entries.citations: (Prov 6:23) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: Bread soured — the word made impure, embittered, and puffed up; the hidden corruption that ferments through the whole lump, purged before Passover and forbidden on God's altar. The NT names it the corrupt doctrine of the Pharisees.
entries.citations: (Lev 2:11; Matt 16:12; 1 Cor 5:7-8) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: The King's jubilee release — out of the slaver's house (sin, Egypt, Babylon) and home to the household, inheritance, and service of God; a change of masters, never the absence of one. Its constitution is the perfect law of liberty; its counterfeit, liberty as license, is a return to bondage.
entries.citations: (Lev 25:10; Isa 61:1; Jas 1:25; 2 Pet 2:19) · see Liberty, ch. 19

entries.definition: Covenant existence — the life the law produces.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: Christ Himself, and the eternal life imparted to believers.
entries.citations: (Deut 30:19-20; Lev 18:5; John 14:6; Matt 7:14) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7

entries.definition: The law lived visibly — good works others can see.
entries.citations: (Prov 6:23; Matt 5:16) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: The devouring ruler or empire — the beast-kingdom at its most royal and most predatory: “as a roaring lion… so is a wicked ruler”; the princes are lions, and Assyria and Babylon “the lions” that scattered the sheep. The figure's rightful holder is the Lion of the tribe of Juda — and in His kingdom the lion is tamed.
entries.citations: (Prov 28:15; Zeph 3:3; Jer 50:17; Ezek 19; Rev 5:5) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: A nation — as the beasts of Daniel's sea are kingdoms, the living creatures in Revelation's sea are peoples.
entries.citations: (Dan 7:3, 17; Rev 8:9; 16:3) · see The Bow, ch. 44

entries.definition: The Spirit and word of God going out to give life.
entries.citations: (Jer 2:13; John 7:38) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: The scattered house of Israel, sought and regathered.
entries.citations: (Matt 15:24) · see Jacob, Israel & Ephraim, ch. 45

entries.definition: The covenant union of God and His people — the one-flesh bond God joins: the wife called by the Husband's name, brought under His wing.
entries.citations: (Gen 2:24; Ezek 16:8; Eph 5:31-32; Rev 19:7) · see Marriage and Divorce, ch. 12

entries.definition: The word obeyed to completeness — “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work”; and the will is the word: where Matthew hears “do the will of my Father,” Luke records the same saying as “hear the word of God, and do it.” Milk and meat are one substance in two states — the word received, and the word done: chewed and tasted as the ear tries words, served in due season, its fruit senses exercised to discern.
entries.citations: (John 4:34; 6:55; 7:17; Matt 12:50; Luke 8:21; Ps 40:8; Job 34:3; Heb 5:14; Matt 24:45) · see Introduction, ch. 1

entries.definition: The word received — teaching another has already digested, swallowed without work; the right first food of babes, given to grow them, and meant to be outgrown at weaning. Churned, it becomes butter — the word worked toward solid food.
entries.citations: (1 Pet 2:2; 1 Cor 3:1-2; Isa 28:9; 7:15; Prov 30:33; Heb 5:12-13) · see Introduction, ch. 1

entries.definition: The instant of decisive action, built on the image of an eye's wink — the unit in which judgment and mercy alike are done, never a slow process: Babylon falls “in a moment… in one day,” and the dead are raised “in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.”
entries.citations: (Isa 47:9; Job 34:20; 1 Cor 15:52) · see The Moment, ch. 38 | (Isa 47:9; Job 34:20; 1 Cor 15:52) · see The Moment, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The faithful witness — the Son, who shines with no light of His own but the Father's reflected, the light that shineth in the world's night; the lesser light that rules the night and marks the appointed times.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the church reflecting Christ's light as the moon reflects the sun.
entries.citations: (Ps 89:37; Rev 1:5; John 1:5; 5:19) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: A kingdom — the seat of ruling authority.
entries.citations: (Jer 51:25; Dan 2:35) · see Mountain, ch. 39

entries.definition: Without covenant covering — exposed in one's breach.
entries.citations: (Ezek 16:8; Gen 3:7) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43

entries.definition: The covenant identity of a house, consisting of 3 things appointed and provided by its Head: the Word (the manna), the covenant law (the stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron's budded rod). A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood; a Name is taken in vain when any one is rejected, replaced, or removed. A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house, coming under His authority, and obeying Him.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the person's character, authority, and reputation.

entries.definition: The gospel’s gathering of all kinds out of the sea of peoples.
entries.citations: (Matt 13:47-48) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: A newly conferred covenant identity under its giver — known, received, and kept only by the one who bears it.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: a new God-given identity and character bestowed on the overcomer.
entries.citations: (Gen 32:28; Isa 62:2-5; 65:15; Rev 2:17) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: The renewed moon — chodesh, from chadash, to renew: the phase of the moon that serves as the sign of the start of the month, and so the name of the month itself. A sign must be watched for: the east gate opens on it for worship, commerce resents it, and Paul files it among the shadows of things to come; which phase renews the month, the Pearl chapter weighs from the letters.
entries.citations: (Ps 81:3; 1 Sam 20:5, 18; Isa 66:23; Ezek 46:1-3; Amos 8:5; Col 2:16-17) · see The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31

entries.definition: The time of darkness — hiding and sleep, when opportunity closes; the children of the night sleep and are drunken, doing their deeds in the dark.
entries.citations: (Gen 1:5; 1 Thess 5:5-7) · see Light and Darkness, ch. 21

entries.definition: A great city of the sea — gentile peoples who repent and rise in judgment.
entries.citations: (Matt 12:41) · see The Sign of Jonah, ch. 4

entries.definition: The hidden quarter — tsaphon, from the root to hide, to lurk: the dark side of the sky, the door the ambush comes by. In the north country the spoilers of Babylon gather — “an assembly of great nations,” the ten allied kings who turn on the seven the whore rules — and in its uttermost recesses, the “sides of the north,” the enemy set his seat.
entries.citations: (Jer 1:14; 50:9, 41; 51:48; Ps 48:2; Isa 14:13; Rev 17:16-18) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35, and Lucifer's Declared Plan, ch. 30

entries.definition: The commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until they govern the life — the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored as proven obedience; light is that obedience made visible as an example to others.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the Holy Spirit — anointing, consecration, and empowering.

entries.definition: Israel, the covenant people.
entries.citations: (Jer 11:16; Hos 9:10) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: The covenant made whole — shalom, from a root meaning to complete, restore, repay: the work of righteousness, the great peace of them that love the law — not the world’s truce and not a feeling (“not as the world giveth”). What the gospel publishes is this peace restored; the counterfeit pronounces it twice over an unkept covenant — “Peace, peace; when there is no peace.”

The one complete light — under the KJV's “rubies” (peninim, Strong's pearl), wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls; and the night sky's one pearl is the full moon (keseh, “fulness,” the letters under “throne” and “time appointed”), governor of the appointed times, the one-pearl gates of the city — the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the kingdom of heaven, worth surrendering everything to gain — or the church, purchased by Christ.
entries.citations: (Prov 3:15; 31:10; Ps 81:3; Prov 7:20; Job 26:9; Ps 104:19; Rev 21:21) · see The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31

entries.definition: The bowed-humble before God — one Hebrew word family behind “poor” and “meek,” and “needy” (evyon) its constant companion; empty-handed toward Him, and so able to receive: the gospel’s hearers and heirs of the kingdom.
entries.citations: (Ps 37:11/Matt 5:5; Isa 61:1/Luke 4:18; Isa 66:2; Jas 2:5; Ps 72:12-13) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: The faithful few who glean the edge — widow, fatherless, stranger, as Ruth did; small by design, refined like gold out of dross, at a fixed ratio traceable from the gleaning law's own geometry to Elijah's seven thousand.
entries.citations: (Ruth 2; 1 Kgs 19:18; Zech 13:8-9; Rom 11:5) · see The Remnant, ch. 15

entries.definition: The self-sufficient who “have need of nothing” — full of self, and so unable to receive; Laodicea's boast, and Smyrna's opposite. The true wealth is being “rich toward God”: faith tried in the fire, and the garment of righteousness.
entries.citations: (Rev 3:17-18; Rev 2:9; Prov 13:7; Luke 12:21) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: Right-living. God is Right-Living by definition — His ways and works are the measure of right. For those under His authority, right-living is the doing of His commandments: the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts. Romans 4 excludes wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience; even complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty. Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, but the gift never renames wrong-living right.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: primarily right standing before God — Christ's imputed righteousness received by faith apart from works — with right-living as its subsequent fruit and evidence.
entries.citations: (Deut 32:4; 6:25; Ps 119:172; 145:17; Luke 17:7-10; Rom 4:4-8; Phil 3:9; Heb 11:8; 1 John 3:7) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6, for the dependent definitions; The End of the Law for Paul's wage, debt, law, and obedience vocabulary; and Garments & Armor, ch. 43, for righteousness given and worn

entries.definition: The covenant — the Rock that followed Israel “was Christ,” the covenant in person; the stone the builders refused, made the cornerstone.
entries.citations: (Deut 32:4; Isa 42:6; 1 Cor 10:4; Ps 118:22) · see Mountain, ch. 39

entries.definition: The countless multitude — grains of the shore beyond number; and so a shifting foundation: to build on the sand is to build on the crowd, not the covenant-rock.
entries.citations: (Gen 22:17; Hos 1:10; Rev 20:8; Matt 7:26) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: The complete seven — six-and-one as a single whole, at every scale the law counts it: the week whose seventh day is the rest, the seventh year that rests the land, the seven-sevens that ring in jubilee. Scripture counts “seven sabbaths complete” and calls the week itself the sabbath; the rest-day is the crown of the unit, one-seventh of what the word names.
entries.citations: (Lev 23:15 with Deut 16:9; Lev 25:2-8; 2 Chr 36:21; Luke 18:12; Matt 28:1; Heb 4:9) · see The Sabbath, ch. 32 | (Lev 23:15 with Deut 16:9; Lev 25:2-8; 2 Chr 36:21; Luke 18:12; Matt 28:1; Heb 4:9) · see The Sabbath, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: Covenant blood made wearable — and counterfeited by those who wear the form without the substance.
entries.citations: (Isa 1:18; Josh 2:18; Heb 9:19; Rev 17:4) · see Garments & Armor, ch. 43 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: Peoples and nations — the restless, unrooted mass below the firmament; and, above it, the gathered waters of heaven: the still sea of glass where the angels and the redeemed stand.
entries.citations: (Rev 17:15; Gen 1:6-8; Ps 148:4; Rev 4:6; 15:2) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: The NAME impressed on its owner — the signet-plate the law sets on the priest's forehead (HOLINESS TO THE LORD), the law bound on hand and between the eyes, stamped by the Spirit on God's servants before judgment; the inscription is quoted: the Lord knoweth them that are his — let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity. The counterfeit takes the same two places.
The word of God, sown in the hearts of men.
entries.citations: (Luke 8:11) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: The deceiver; the one who strips the covenant covering.
entries.citations: (Gen 3:1) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The covering of a greater presence — refuge under the Almighty's wings, a kingdom's protection over its people, the outline a coming body casts ahead of itself. Good to dwell in — not the gloom it is read as; the KJV itself renders the word “defence”.
entries.citations: (Ps 91:1; Num 14:9; Col 2:17) · see Shadow, ch. 17

entries.definition: The covenant people, who hear the Shepherd's voice and follow.
entries.citations: (John 10:27) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: The demanding place — from sha'al, to demand: mortality's claim on all flesh, swallowing righteous and wicked alike, personified with a mouth, gates, and bars. Its dead sleep in silence until it is made to give them back; then it is itself destroyed — “O grave, I will be thy destruction.” Distinct from Gehenna, the judgment.
entries.citations: (Gen 37:35; Ps 16:10; Eccl 9:5; Isa 5:14; Hos 13:14; Rev 20:13-14) · see Heaven and Hell, ch. 16

entries.definition: An earthly kingdom, city, state, or governed political body riding upon the sea of peoples: its rulers guide it, its inhabitants and servants crew it, its armies defend it, and its wealth is carried as cargo. Christ needs no constructed body beneath Him: He walks upon the sea directly, and when He sails with His disciples the vessel comes under its true Head. The ship may be broken while its people survive.
A prophecy given in advance — often a prophet's lived story — whose fulfillment testifies; not a wonder performed on demand.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: a miraculous act pointing to God's power and Christ's identity.
entries.citations: (Isa 7:14; Ezek 24:24; Luke 11:30) · see Signs and Similitudes, ch. 3

entries.definition: The transgression of the law — Scripture's own definition: “sin is the transgression of the law”; where no law is, there is no transgression, and by the law is the knowledge of sin.
entries.citations: (1 John 3:4; Rom 4:15; 3:20; 7:7) · see Grace, Mercy & the Gift, ch. 24

entries.definition: A spiritual name of Jerusalem — the prophets address her rulers so to their faces: “Hear the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom… ye people of Gomorrah”; Ezekiel calls Sodom her sister and Jerusalem the worse; and Revelation writes the name on “the great city… where also our Lord was crucified.”
entries.citations: (Isa 1:10; Ezek 16:46-48; Rev 11:8) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The righteous, who rule the night with the Son — “they that be wise shall shine… as the stars for ever”; the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, gathered into the twelve constellations, the Mazzaroth.
entries.citations: (Dan 12:3; Ps 136:9; Gen 37:9; Rev 12:1; Job 38:32) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: A covenant cut by God — for a covenant is cut (Hebrew karat) — grown into the kingdom that breaks the world-empires and fills the earth.
entries.citations: (Dan 2:34-35, 44-45; Gen 15:17-18; Deut 9:10; Col 2:11) · see Mountain, ch. 39

entries.definition: The nations in turmoil — the raging sea, stilled at Christ's word, “Peace, be still”.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: divine judgment, and the trials of life which Christ has power to calm.
entries.citations: (Ps 65:7; Isa 17:12-13; Mark 4:39; Luke 21:25) · see Sea & Waters, ch. 40

entries.definition: A non-citizen of God's commonwealth — one outside the covenant, drawn in, or, once in, made a stranger to the world.
entries.citations: (Eph 2:12, 19) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: The Father, the source of light, from which every lesser light is drawn; the righteous shall shine as the sun in His kingdom.
entries.citations: (Ps 84:11; Gen 37:9; Matt 13:43) · see Sun, Moon & Stars, ch. 29

entries.definition: The unclean beast par excellence — the one beast in the law wearing the outward sign without the inward work: the hoof parted, the cud never chewed. The nation outside the covenant that tramples what is holy — pearls under their feet, the holy city under the Gentiles, the washed sow back in the mire.
entries.citations: (Lev 11:7; Deut 14:8; Matt 7:6; Rev 11:2; Isa 66:17; 2 Pet 2:22) · see The Other White Meat, ch. 48

entries.definition: War and the word of judgment — the great sword that takes peace from the earth; the flaming sword that guards the way.
entries.citations: (Rev 6:4; Gen 3:24) · see The Four Winds, ch. 34

entries.definition: The prophet that teacheth lies — Isaiah's own decode, with head and tail already defined by the covenant: obedience makes Israel “the head, and not the tail,” and the curse inverts it. The dragon fells a third of the stars with its tail — the led destroyed by the misleading — and the trumpet armies' serpent-tails “had heads”: the liar enthroned. Moses is told to seize the serpent exactly there.
entries.citations: (Isa 9:15-16; Deut 28:13, 44; Rev 12:4; 9:19; Ex 4:4) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The counterfeit sown among the wheat by the enemy — a weed that mimics the true grain until the harvest, then is bound in bundles and burned; the children of the wicked one, distinct from the winnowed chaff.
entries.citations: (Matt 13:25-30, 38-40) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: The stronghold raised by a Name around its house — refuge, watchtower, and lighthouse in one: high to see danger, giving light to guide the house, and covered to shelter those who come inside. A strong tower is an intact Name protecting its people; an unfinished tower is a Name begun without depth to endure its cost; a fallen tower is a covenant stronghold broken, emptied, or judged.
entries.citations: (Prov 18:10; Ex 13:21; Isa 4:5-6; Hab 2:1; Gen 11:1-8; Luke 14:28-30; Matt 13:20-21; Luke 13:4-5) · see The Tower | (Prov 18:10; Ex 13:21; Isa 4:5-6; Hab 2:1; Gen 11:1-8; Luke 14:28-30; Matt 13:20-21; Luke 13:4-5) · see The Tower

entries.definition: A nation or people.
entries.citations: (Dan 4:22; Rom 11:17) · see Trees, ch. 41

entries.definition: God's law — the standard.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: Christ Himself, and God's word — the gospel that sets free.
entries.citations: (Ps 119:142; 2 John 4) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7

entries.definition: The tassels bound to the corners of the garment; looking upon them reminds the wearer of all the LORD's commandments, to do them.
entries.citations: (Num 15:38-39) · see Wings, ch. 13

entries.definition: Discernment of good from evil, gained by departing from evil — “a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”.
entries.citations: (Job 28:28; Ps 111:10) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: The low and humbled — the opposite of the mountain-kingdom; “every valley shall be exalted”.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: the low seasons of trial and death, set against the mountaintop.
entries.citations: (Isa 40:4) · see Mountain, ch. 39 — derived in the digital edition’s symbol study at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The espoused — betrothed to one husband with the wedding still ahead: covenant standing, not attainment; the law counts a betrothed virgin already a wife, the prophets call the ten-tribe house re-espoused after her divorce “the virgin of Israel,” and virgins plural are the bride’s companions who follow her in — the opposite of the harlot who goes after many.
entries.citations: (Deut 22:23-24; Joel 1:8; Jer 31:4, 21; Amos 5:2; Ps 45:14-15; 2 Cor 11:2; Matt 25:1) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: The words of the one who speaks; the Shepherd's voice is His words.
entries.citations: (John 10:27) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: Covenant conduct — the walk.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: Jesus Himself as the one way to the Father; the narrow way against the broad.
entries.citations: (Jer 6:16; Matt 7:14) · see The Way, the Truth & the Life, ch. 7

entries.definition: Salvation — the covenant's enclosure: “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation”; God Himself “a wall of fire round about.” The counterfeit is self-built — wealth's high wall “in his own conceit,” and the whitewashed wall of false peace that the storm flattens.
entries.citations: (Isa 60:18; Zech 2:5; Prov 18:11; Ezek 13:10-15) · see The Parable of the Vineyard | (Isa 60:18; Zech 2:5; Prov 18:11; Ezek 13:10-15) · see The Parable of the Vineyard, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: A seven — shavua, a unit of sevens, and not only of days: Laban decodes it in the text — “Fulfil her week… yet seven other years” — and Jacob serves seven years for the week named; the jubilee is counted as “seven sabbaths of years,” and Daniel’s seventy weeks are sevens of years — unpointed, seventy sevens that open into seventy jubilees. The Feast of Weeks runs the same count in days — seven sevens to the fiftieth — the jubilee modeled a day for a year.
entries.citations: (Gen 29:27-28; Lev 23:15-16; 25:8; Dan 9:24-25) · see Daniel Unsealed, ch. 36

entries.definition: The sea at the back — the Hebrew for west is “sea” (yam): Israel faces east, so the west is “the hinder sea,” what lies behind; and as far as the east is from the west, so far are the transgressions removed.
entries.citations: (Zech 14:8; Joel 2:20; Ps 103:12) · see The Fall of Babylon, ch. 35

entries.definition: The children of the kingdom — the good grain gathered into the barn at the harvest.
entries.citations: (Matt 13:38; 3:12) · see Grass, ch. 42

entries.definition: God's covenant people cut off from their Husband.
entries.citations: (Lam 1:1; Isa 54:5) · see Orphans, Widows & the Fatherless, ch. 14

entries.definition: Spirit — ruach.
entries.citations: (Zech 6:5) · see The Four Winds, ch. 34

entries.definition: The vineyard's reckoning — where the fruit a people has borne is pressed out and rendered to the Owner, in one of two vintages: presses that “burst out with new wine” when the grapes are good; the growers themselves trodden — “the great winepress of the wrath of God” — and blood for wine, when the vintage is wickedness.
entries.citations: (Isa 5:2, 7; Prov 3:10; Joel 2:24; 3:13; Lam 1:15; Isa 63:3; Rev 14:19-20) · see The Parable of the Vineyard | (Isa 5:2, 7; Prov 3:10; Joel 2:24; 3:13; Lam 1:15; Isa 63:3; Rev 14:19-20) · see The Parable of the Vineyard, in the free digital edition at TimeTested.Bible

entries.definition: The covenant edge — wing, skirt, border, corner — where the reminder of the law is bound and refuge is found.
entries.citations: (Ezek 16:8) · see Wings, ch. 13

entries.definition: The fear of the LORD lived out — the doing of the commandments; “the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom”.
entries.citations: (Prov 9:10; Ps 111:10; Deut 4:6) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: One who hears God's word and does it, who fears the LORD.
entries.citations: (Matt 7:24; Ps 111:10) · see The Fool and the Wise, ch. 20

entries.definition: To bow down and serve — homage in the body, allegiance in the life; the fear of the LORD made visible, kept at His appointed times, on His terms. Not the song service: Scripture separates worship from singing in single scenes.
entries.citations: (Ex 20:5; Matt 4:10/Deut 6:13; 2 Chr 20:18-19; Rev 14:7) · see Worship, ch. 22

entries.definition: A turning — shanah, written on the root to change, repeat, return: one complete cycle of time, at whatever scale the count is running — Jeremiah’s seventy “years” close only as seventy jubilees, and a thousand years pass as a day.
entries.citations: (Jer 25:11-12; Dan 9:2, 24; Ps 90:4) · see Daniel Unsealed, ch. 36
